claim: The Inference Scheduler component was renamed to 'llm-d Router', and core Endpoint Picker (EPP) code plus the InferenceObjective and InferenceModelRewrite APIs have been merged into the llm-d/llm-d-router repo from kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension (GIE), which now hosts only the InferencePool API and the Endpoint Picker Protocol definition.
stance_target: current architecture and repo boundaries of llm-d routing components
scope_conditions: llm-d-router repo README, current as of release v0.10.0 (Aug 17, 2026)
quoted_support: Core Endpoint Picker (EPP) code and the `InferenceObjective` and `InferenceModelRewrite` APIs have been merged into this repository from Gateway API Inference Extension (GIE). The GIE repository now exclusively hosts the `InferencePool` API—an extension of the Kubernetes Gateway API—and defines the Endpoint Picker Protocol.

claim: The llm-d Router supports two deployment modes: Standalone Mode (self-managed Envoy, sidecar or service topology, no Gateway API infra required) and Gateway Mode, where EPP acts as a backend for an InferencePool referenced by an HTTPRoute on a shared Gateway; Gateway Mode is the recommended mode for production.
stance_target: deployment topology options for the llm-d router
quoted_support: The recommended mode for production environments, leveraging the official Gateway API. In this mode, the EPP acts as a backend for an `InferencePool`, which is referenced by an `HTTPRoute` on a shared `Gateway`.

claim: The EPP integrates with L7 proxies (e.g. Envoy) via the ext-proc protocol, and the only supported request_body_mode/response_body_mode for a self-configured Envoy is FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED.
stance_target: wire-protocol constraints for integrating a custom proxy/backend with the EPP
quoted_support: The project provides tools for automatic Envoy installation. However, if you install or configure it yourself, please note that the only supported request_body_mode and response_body_mode is `FULL_DUPLEX_STREAMED`

claim: A merged PR (#2476) added ATOM (AMD GPU inference engine) as a built-in metrics-extraction engine, letting a deployment add a new backend engine type purely by labeling pods llm-d.ai/engine-type: atom rather than writing a custom engineConfigs block, following the same atom: metric-prefix convention as existing sglang: and trtllm_ engines.
stance_target: the llm-d router's existing plugin/label conventions already generalize to new backend engine types with minimal code
scope_conditions: llm-d-router repo, PR #2476, merged into main by Sep 11, 2026
quoted_support: Registering it here means a deployment only has to label its pods with `llm-d.ai/engine-type: atom`, rather than carrying an engineConfigs block that restates metric names the engine already fixes.

claim: PR #2620, 'feat(helm): support structured plugin config', merged into llm-d-router main on Sep 11, 2026, adds structured Helm-chart support for configuring EPP plugins.
stance_target: the router's Helm chart configuration surface for plugins is actively evolving toward more structured/extensible config

claim: The Architecture Documentation (docs/architecture.md) is the canonical source for router architecture, routing logic, and the different filter/scorer plugins; the Disaggregation Documentation (docs/disaggregation.md) covers the Disaggregation Sidecar for P/D and E/P/D lifecycles.
stance_target: location of authoritative design docs for router internals relevant to backend customization
quoted_support: For more details on the router architecture, routing logic, and different plugins (filters and scorers), see the Architecture Documentation.
